title: Hoatzin chicks have claws on their wings, and the adults digest leaves like cows
body: The hoatzin lives in swamps and riverside forests of the Amazon and Orinoco basins and eats mostly leaves. Like a cow, it relies on bacteria to ferment that tough food, but in an enlarged two-chambered crop rather than a stomach with several chambers. Its chicks hatch with **two claws on each wing** and use them to scramble through branches over the water. When danger comes, a chick drops into the river, swims underwater, then climbs back up to its nest with those clawed wings.

cover.alt: A hoatzin perched on a bare branch against a blue sky, with a spiky orange crest, red eye and blue bare skin around it

slides.question: Out of every 10 parts of plant fibre it eats, up to how many can a hoatzin digest?
slides.explanation: Up to 70%. Bacteria in its crop break down the leaves, much as microbes do in the stomach of a cow.

slides.heading: The price of a leaf diet
slides.text: The crop that does the fermenting is so large that it pushes aside the flight muscles and the keel of the breastbone. That makes the hoatzin a poor flier. At as little as 700 g, it is the smallest animal known to digest by foregut fermentation. Locals call it the stinkbird for its manure-like smell.

left.label: The old idea
left.text: The wing claws were compared with those of the fossil bird *Archaeopteryx*, as if left over from ancient ancestors.

right.label: Today's view
right.text: Researchers now think the claws are of more recent origin, and may be a secondary adaptation rather than a relic.

slides.heading: Which one is NOT true of the hoatzin?
items: It ferments leaves in its crop
slides.explanation: The claws disappear by the time the bird is an adult. The other three are all true.
